provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Care family batch. Health-regulated: no outcome claims, no invented credentials, consent-only galleries. Bigger tickets than the rest of the family, so builds and add-ons run higher. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Lines, volume, skin texture and sun damage, each mapped to the injectable, filler, laser or microneedling options the clinic offers, with appointment length and the downtime the provider describes
pageStructurePlus.why: Med spa clients arrive with a concern, not a treatment name. A page that starts from the concern gets them to the right consultation instead of a wrong booking.

pageStructurePlus.contains: The medical director's name and [licence type], each injector's [credential] as the clinic publishes it, and how the good-faith exam works before a first neuromodulator or filler appointment
pageStructurePlus.why: Clients compare med spas on who holds the syringe. A plain supervision page answers the question they are too polite to ask on the phone.

pageStructurePlus.contains: How the clinic prices injectables: per unit, per syringe of filler or per treatment area, with the clinic's own ranges or bracketed placeholders, plus how membership pricing changes the bill
pageStructurePlus.why: Injectable prices are quoted three different ways across town. The clinic that explains its own method plainly wins the shopper who is comparing tabs.

pageStructurePlus.contains: What the provider will ask at the consultation: medications, pregnancy, recent dental work or procedures, allergies, and why those details stay off the website form
pageStructurePlus.why: Careful clients want to know the clinic screens before it injects. Saying so, without collecting health details on a web form, reads as the safer chair.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Only pictures the client signed off on, unretouched, each labelled with the treatment, the number of sessions and the timeframe, beside a plain note that results differ from person to person
pageStructurePlus.why: Results pictures are what aesthetics shoppers look for first, and the clinic carries the risk if a gallery overpromises or shows someone without consent.

openers.line: Your med spa's Google listing has hours and a phone number but no website, so someone in {City} comparing injectables clinics can't see who you are before they call.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what would sit behind that button for the med spa: {demo-link}

openers.angle: Booking app as the whole site
openers.line: Your bio link drops straight into a booking app with treatment names and no explanation. A first-time injectables client wants to know who injects and how pricing works before they pick a slot.
openers.hook: Tap their bio link and note where it lands: a booking app, a link page or a Facebook page.
openers.linkLine: A med spa page that explains first, then books: {demo-link}

openers.line: The aesthetics site on your listing still shows a treatment special from last spring and an injector who seems to have moved on. Careful clients read that as a clinic that isn't paying attention.
openers.hook: Open the site and find one stale detail: an old special, a departed injector, a dead booking button. Note it.
openers.linkLine: The same clinic, current and calm: {demo-link}

openers.line: I opened your med spa site on my phone and the treatment menu ran off the side of the screen. Most people researching filler do it on a phone, late, in private.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: The med spa, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way to ask for an injectables consultation on your page without calling during clinic hours. Nervous first-timers would rather fill in a short request and hear back.
openers.hook: Look for a consult form anywhere: site, listing, bio. If the only route is a phone call, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A consultation request built for first-time injectables clients: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your consented results posts are scattered between product promos and holiday hours. A clinic gallery sorted by treatment, labelled honestly, would do the explaining for you.
openers.hook: Find one results post that clearly names the treatment. Check the caption mentions consent before you use this angle.
openers.linkLine: A consent-led results gallery, sorted by treatment: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your Google reviews keep mentioning how unhurried the injector was at the consultation. That's the exact worry a first-time med spa client has, and it isn't on any page they'd read.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about the consultation or the injector. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your reviews beside the consultation button: {demo-link}

openers.line: Brides and holiday-party guests start asking about injectables and skin treatments weeks ahead. A clinic page that explains timing and books the consult catches them before they call around.
openers.hook: Use this in late summer for holiday parties or January for spring weddings. Name the season.
openers.linkLine: A med spa page ready for event season: {demo-link}

openers.line: Most people read about filler and wrinkle-relaxing injections at night, long after your front desk goes home. Right now there's nothing to read and nowhere to request a consult.
openers.hook: Look for comments asking 'how much' or 'do you do consults' that sat unanswered. Note one.
openers.linkLine: A med spa page that takes consult requests at midnight: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring an aesthetic injector. The good ones check the clinic's website and its supervision setup before they apply.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring story or job post for an injector, aesthetician or front desk. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A med spa page with a careers section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews mention clients driving in from {Neighborhood} and further out for injectables. A page that says where the clinic is and where to park makes that drive feel planned.
openers.hook: Scan reviews for neighbourhoods or towns clients mention. Use the real name in place of {Neighborhood}.
openers.linkLine: A med spa page for clients coming from further out: {demo-link}

openers.line: You mention a membership in your stories, but there's nowhere to read what it includes. A clear membership page does a lot of the selling for a med spa.
openers.hook: Check stories and highlights for 'membership', 'VIP' or payment-plan mentions. If there's no page explaining it, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A med spa membership page that explains itself: {demo-link}

openers.line: Nothing I could find online says who the medical director is or what training your injectors hold. That's the first thing a cautious aesthetics client looks for.
openers.hook: Look for 'medical director', 'RN', 'NP' or training mentions in their bio and posts. Never invent a credential.
openers.linkLine: Who injects and who supervises, stated plainly: {demo-link}

openers.line: It sounds like most of your injectables clients come from friends of clients. Those referrals still search the med spa's name before they book, and right now they find very little.
openers.hook: Look for posts thanking clients for referrals or reviews saying 'my friend sent me'. Quote it.
openers.linkLine: Where a referred med spa client would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is careful aesthetics work, and the caption explains it well. A treatment page built around it would answer the next client's questions too.
openers.hook: Pick their newest consented results post or treatment explainer and name it exactly: the treatment and the area.
openers.linkLine: That treatment, explained on its own page: {demo-link}

Would you like me to send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case my message got buried under client DMs. Here's the sample med spa site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has treatments by concern, a consultation request that keeps health details off the form, and a supervision section with placeholders for your real credentials. If it's not for you, say so and I won't message again.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for med spas and injectables clinics here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"Easy to miss between appointments. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} with treatments by concern, a consultation request and a page on who injects, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and treatment menu changes. For a clinic like yours I'd normally quote about {Build Price}."
"Nothing on it makes a result claim. Every credential and price comes from you, and anything you haven't given me stays a bracketed placeholder."
"Could we take fifteen minutes after your last client one evening this week?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears."

objections.objection: We already get messages from marketing agencies every day.
objections.handler: "I know, med spas are pitched constantly. I'm not selling ads or a lead program. It's one site you own, built so a careful client trusts the clinic before the consult."

objections.objection: Our booking app already has our treatment menu.
objections.handler: "It lists treatments. It can't explain who supervises, how unit pricing works or what the consultation is like. The site answers those first, then hands the client to your booking app."

objections.objection: We have to be careful about what we say online.
objections.handler: "Agreed, and that's how it's built. No outcome claims, no invented credentials, consented pictures only, and you or your medical director sign off every page before it goes live."

objections.objection: All our clients come from Instagram.
objections.handler: "Instagram starts the interest. The site is where they check who injects, what it costs and how to book a consult without waiting on a DM. It links straight back to your grid."
"Then build the site with the rebrand, not after it. I can work from the new name and colours, and launch when the signage changes."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because of the treatment pages, the supervision page and the consult request. A handful of new injectables clients covers it."

email.subject: A site for {Business Name}

sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm taking the {Business Name} med spa demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to leave it up a little longer? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner}, holiday party season is when injectables consults pile up, and the clinics with a clear consult page take the calm ones first. Thought of you.

The sample site is still here whenever you want it, and nothing's changed on price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a few new injectables clients, not to the clinic's ad budget. Med spas are pitched big retainers daily, and a fixed site price stands out.
Price treatment pages by concern, not by product. One lines-and-volume page carries more than five thin product pages.
The supervision and credentials page is its own line, because it needs the medical director's review before it ships.
Never write the clinic's prices yourself. Quote the pricing explainer with bracketed placeholders and charge for the structure.
Consent records and a results gallery cost more than a plain gallery. Price the consent step, not the picture count.
Keep monthly add-ons below the price of a single filler syringe. Clinics compare every monthly line to a treatment.
Sell membership and event-season pages ahead of the season, never in the rush.

lineItems.description: Max when the concern maps to several treatments, each with appointment length, downtime as described by the provider and who should not book.
Max with several injectors, the good-faith exam explained, and a review round with the medical director.
Max when it covers per-unit, per-syringe and per-area methods side by side with membership pricing.
Max with treatment filters, consent records tied to each picture and a takedown request route for clients.
Max with several membership levels, a comparison table and recurring billing hooked to the clinic's payment account.
Max when it routes by treatment interest and explains which health questions are asked in person, not on the form.
Max when treatment pages, pricing explainer and consult request are all translated and reviewed by a bilingual staff member.

whatElseYouSell.name: Consented treatment content day at the clinic
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One clinic day filming the treatment rooms, the injectors and consenting clients gives the med spa a season of calm, honest posts."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, booked on a day with clients who have signed a media consent form in advance.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep for the med spa
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Weekly posts on the clinic's Google profile naming the treatment, the injector and the hours, so people searching for a med spa nearby see a busy, careful clinic."

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests after each treatment visit
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A few days after the appointment, once any swelling has settled, the client gets a short note asking how the injectables visit went and whether they'd review it."

whatElseYouSell.name: Event-season consultation campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A planned push in the weeks before holiday parties and spring weddings, pointing people to an aesthetics consult instead of a last-minute walk-in."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in August for the holidays, or December for wedding season.

whatElseYouSell.name: Monthly treatment explainer reels
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Short explainers where your injector walks through what a filler or laser appointment actually involves, scripted with you and checked before they post."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, if they say content is the part they never get to.

whatElseYouSell.name: Clinic signage and treatment menu cards
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A treatment-room menu card and a front-desk sign with the consult code, so the client in the chair can book their friend a med spa consult."

whatElseYouSell.name: Client newsletter for the aesthetics practice
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One calm email a month to existing aesthetics clients: new treatments, injector availability and membership news. No countdown timers."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once the client list is in one place.

whatElseYouSell.name: Neighbourhood pages for the clinic
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A page for each neighbourhood your injectables clients drive in from, with the route, parking and the consult button."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 4, once reviews show where clients come from.

withoutAI.route: The plastic surgery practice that refers clients
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The surgeon who sends you non-surgical clients has a dated practice site. I build for clinics with careful medical copy rules already."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Surgeons and med spas trade referrals constantly. A med spa owner vouching for you is the only warm way into a surgical office.

withoutAI.route: The aesthetics product distributor's regional rep
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Your injectables rep runs training evenings for every clinic in the region and signs people up by text. Introduce me and I'll build the event calendar."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Distributors fund education to keep clinics ordering, and their clinic list is your prospect list.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The academy where your injectors trained sells courses from a single flyer page. A course site with dates and prerequisites fills those seats."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Training academies sell to nurses and practitioners who research carefully. The clinic's injectors are trusted alumni.

withoutAI.route: Bridal boutiques that send brides for skin prep
withoutAI.whoPays: The boutique, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The bridal boutique that recommends your med spa for pre-wedding skin treatments needs a site that books fittings online. I build those too."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Bridal vendors pass the same client along a chain. One trusted aesthetics clinic opens the boutique's door.

withoutAI.route: Cosmetic dentists in the same plaza
withoutAI.whoPays: The dental office, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The cosmetic dentist next to the clinic shares half your aesthetics clients and has the same consult-first problem. I'd build theirs on the same calm layout."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Same affluent client, same regulated copy care, and the plaza makes the introduction natural.

withoutAI.route: Lash and brow studios that refer facial clients
withoutAI.whoPays: Each studio, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The lash studio that sends you facial and skin clients books from a bio link. I'll give them a small site that points clients back to your med spa too."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Small beauty studios trade referrals with the nearest med spa. A shared client base makes the second sale easy.

withAI.route: Course enquiry assistant for the injector academy
withAI.pitchLine: "Nurses asking about injector courses get answers on dates, prerequisites and fees from the academy's own handbook, and the academy gets a qualified enquiry."
withAI.whyItWorks: Academies answer the same course questions every night. An assistant limited to their handbook is a contained, easy yes.

withAI.route: Logistics assistant for the referring surgical practice
withAI.pitchLine: "The surgical office's after-hours questions about parking, forms and consult fees get answered from approved text, and anything clinical goes to the front desk."
withAI.whyItWorks: Practices want fewer logistics calls without any clinical risk. Approved answers only is the line they need to hear.

withAI.route: Clinic locator for the aesthetics distributor
withAI.pitchLine: "Consumers ask which med spas near them carry a treatment line. A locator that matches them to trained accounts keeps those clinics loyal to the distributor."
withAI.whyItWorks: It gives the distributor's clinics new clients, which is worth more to them than a rebate.

withAI.route: Bridal beauty timeline planner for the boutique
withAI.pitchLine: "Brides enter the wedding date and the boutique's planner lays out fittings, hair trials and when to book a med spa consult, from the boutique's own vendor list."
withAI.whyItWorks: Boutiques want to look organised and keep vendor partners close. The med spa sits on that list.

withAI.route: Consult-request assistant for the cosmetic dentist
withAI.pitchLine: "The same consult flow you built for the med spa answers the dentist's late-night veneer questions from approved text and drops a request on their calendar."
withAI.whyItWorks: You already built the same consult flow for the med spa. A neighbouring office is configuration, not a new build.

withAI.route: Refill reminder texts for the lash studio
withAI.pitchLine: "The lash studio's clients get a refill nudge written in the tech's voice when their set is due, adapted from the med spa's treatment reminders."
withAI.whyItWorks: Small studios can't build this themselves, and the med spa's version proves it works on a shared client.

softwareAI.name: Treatment-interval rebooking reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A wrinkle-relaxer client hears from the med spa when the provider's usual interval comes round, not on a random Tuesday."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs the treatment list with the intervals the medical director sets, and access to the booking calendar.

softwareAI.name: Deposits for consults and long treatment slots
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Laser series and filler appointments take a deposit at booking, so a no-show in a long aesthetics slot still pays something."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: At build, or the first time they mention a no-show. Needs their deposit and cancellation policy and a payment account.

softwareAI.name: Price and availability responder for clinic DMs
softwareAI.pitchLine: "'How much per unit' and 'any consults Thursday' get an answer from the clinic's approved pricing text, and anything about health or suitability is handed to a person."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the approved pricing explainer, booking access and a list of topics it must never answer. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Membership billing and benefits tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Med spa members are billed monthly, their banked treatment credits are tracked, and the front desk sees what each member has left."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the membership rules, current member list and a payment account.

softwareAI.name: Post-visit check-in texts with the clinic's aftercare sheet
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The day after an injectables visit, the client gets the clinic's own approved aftercare sheet and the number to call with a concern."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs aftercare sheets signed off by the medical director, per treatment. Sends only approved text, never advice.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for the aesthetics clinic
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each med spa review gets a warm reply drafted for approval, and it never confirms that the reviewer was a client or names their treatment."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, alongside review requests. Needs their reply tone and privacy rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Consent form and photo release tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every results picture the med spa posts is tied to a signed release, with the date and the uses the client agreed to."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their release wording, reviewed by their own adviser, and a habit of asking at checkout.

softwareAI.name: After-hours phone receptionist for the med spa
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Calls after the clinic closes get answered, consults get booked, and any caller describing a reaction is told to contact the provider's on-call line or emergency services."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, once they trust you. Needs policies, booking access and the medical director's escalation wording. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Injectable lot and expiry log
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each vial and syringe is logged with its lot number and expiry, so the clinic knows what's on the shelf and what's running out."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their current stock sheet and the person who receives deliveries. Keeps stock only, not patient records.

softwareAI.name: Lapsed med spa client win-back
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Clients who haven't been into the med spa in a while get a quiet note with the current injector schedule and a consult link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs visit history from the booking system and an opt-out rule.

softwareAI.name: Which-consult-to-book quiz
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A visitor describes the aesthetics concern in their own words and is pointed to the right consultation type, never told what treatment they need."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the concern-to-consult map approved by the medical director. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Injector and treatment room schedule board
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which injector, which laser room and which hours are booked across the week, so the med spa stops double-booking the one machine."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, for clinics with several injectors or a laser room. Needs staff schedules and the room list.

softwareAI.name: Caption drafts with a claims check
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Post a treatment explainer and get a caption in the clinic's voice, with any promise-of-results wording flagged before it goes up."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs a few past captions and the clinic's list of words it won't use. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Gift card and treatment package store
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Facial and skin treatment gift cards on the med spa site, ready for December and Mother's Day."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, before a gifting season. Needs the packages they'll sell and a payment account.

softwareAI.name: Promotion wording checker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Before an injectables special goes out by email or post, it's checked against the clinic's own advertising rules and anything risky is flagged for a person."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs the clinic's written advertising rules from their own adviser. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Injector commission and payout report
softwareAI.pitchLine: "For med spas paying injectors on production: who treated what, retail included, at the end of every pay period."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, only for clinics with staff injectors. Needs commission rules and booking data.

softwareAI.name: Front-desk policy answer search
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New front-desk staff search the med spa's own written policies on deposits, memberships and pre-appointment instructions instead of interrupting an injector."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs written policies, with every answer approved before launch. Front-desk topics only. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Waitlist texts when an aesthetics slot opens
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a filler client drops out, people who asked to see that injector sooner are offered the opening by text, first reply wins."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs booking access and a waitlist people opted into.

softwareAI.name: Member drop-off early warning
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Med spa members who've stopped using their credits are flagged with a suggested personal note, before they cancel the membership."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 7, once membership billing has a few months of data. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Multi-clinic numbers dashboard
softwareAI.pitchLine: "For owners with a second med spa: consults, treatments, memberships and injector hours side by side for each location."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9, only when they open or buy a second clinic. Needs booking and payment exports from both.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the consult and consent tools for independent med spas
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a consult request, a consent tracker and interval reminders for one med spa. Every independent injector juggles the same three binders."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first clinic paid for the workflow. Independent med spas are numerous and talk to each other at training events.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "You supervise dozens of med spas. A site template with a compliant supervision page and consult flow is something every one of them needs."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: These organisations already hold the clinic relationships and care about compliant copy. One contract reaches many clinics.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each med spa location needs its own injector bios and consult calendar under one brand. I build the location template once and roll it out."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One approval at head office becomes many location builds on the same template.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Trained-provider locator for an aesthetics product maker
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Consumers want an injector who trained on your line. A locator tied to your course records sends them to the right clinic."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Manufacturers train injectors and want that training to sell product. The med spa client shows you know the consult workflow.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer every member clinic a med spa site template with a supervision page and a claims-safe treatment menu as a member benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need renewal reasons, and compliant marketing is a constant worry for their members.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: White-label med spa template for agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency runs ads for med spas and patches together landing pages. License my clinic template with the consult flow and supervision page built in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies own the med spa relationship; you sell them the regulated build they don't want to learn.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Graduate launch kit for injector training academies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every nurse injector who finishes your course leaves with a starter clinic page and a consult request ready to switch on."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Academies sell career outcomes. A launch kit is a recurring contract and a pipeline of future clinic clients.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Dermatology groups adding an aesthetics wing
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your practice is adding injectables and lasers alongside medical dermatology. The aesthetics side needs its own consult-first site with your supervision stated plainly."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Groups splitting cosmetic from medical work need a separate front door, and a working med spa build is the proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Insurance brokers who cover med spas
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your med spa clients keep asking what they can safely say online. A resource hub of claims-safe page templates makes your book stickier."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Brokers want fewer claims and more renewals. Careful marketing templates serve both.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Day spas and wellness centres adding injectables
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your day spa is bringing in a nurse injector. The injectables side needs supervision, screening and consult pages your massage menu never had."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Spas expanding into medical aesthetics don't know the copy rules. You've already solved them once.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: The same med spa build in the next metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: New clinics in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I keep to one med spa per part of {City}. Clinics an hour away don't compete with mine, and the aesthetics template is ready."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse the regulated copy, the template and the finished clinic proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "An agency started your med spa rebuild and went quiet halfway. I can finish it on a clinic setup I've already shipped."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Stuck clinics have budget set aside and a deadline. They want someone who has done a med spa before.

upsellLadder.offer: Med spa site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The med spa site and the care plan go on one contract, so a new injector or a price change is a text to me."

upsellLadder.offer: Deposits for consults and long treatment slots
upsellLadder.trigger: They mention a no-show on a laser series or filler appointment.
upsellLadder.line: "That empty laser slot is exactly what a deposit at booking stops."

upsellLadder.trigger: The site has been live a month and the calendar shows injectables clients drifting past their usual interval.
upsellLadder.line: "Your injectables clients are due back on a rhythm. Let's remind them on time and ask the happy ones for a review."

upsellLadder.offer: Consented treatment content day at the clinic
upsellLadder.trigger: The results gallery still shows only a few consented treatment pictures.
upsellLadder.line: "One clinic day with consenting clients fills the med spa gallery honestly for a season."

upsellLadder.offer: Price and availability responder for clinic DMs
upsellLadder.trigger: They say the front desk spends evenings answering 'how much per unit' messages.
upsellLadder.line: "Those per-unit pricing DMs get answered from your approved text while the clinic is closed."

upsellLadder.trigger: They are selling memberships but tracking credits in a spreadsheet.
upsellLadder.line: "Your med spa members deserve better than a spreadsheet. Let's bill and track their credits properly."

upsellLadder.offer: Consent form and photo release tracker
upsellLadder.trigger: They ask whether they can post a client's results picture they took months ago.
upsellLadder.line: "If you're not sure a results picture has a signed release, the clinic needs the tracker before the next post."

upsellLadder.offer: Introduction to the referring plastic surgery practice
upsellLadder.trigger: They mention a surgeon who sends them non-surgical clients and asked who built the med spa site.
upsellLadder.line: "The surgeon who sends you injectables clients asked about the site. Would you introduce me?"
